subject: SentryHealth pilot: Redwood eval setup, dataset format, scoring & next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily@sentryhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: SentryHealth pilot: Redwood eval setup, dataset format, scoring & next steps

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum:

Summary of goals
- Run a short, customer-specific evaluation of model fit for your triage assistant (clinical intake summarization + risk flags).
- Objective: validate whether an off-the-shelf open model plus Redwood runtime meets SentryHealth's accuracy and latency constraints for production.

What we recommend for the pilot
- Models to try (priority order): Redwood-13B-fp16 (baseline), Redwood-7B-quant (low-cost option), and an evaluation run with Llama2-13b-chat (for sensitivity comparison).
- Dataset size: 1,200 labeled examples (split 70/15/15 for train/val/test) — we can run on your smaller sample first (200) for a rapid smoke test.
- Prompt bank: included in attachment (sentry_sample_prompts.csv) with canonical instruction templates + 8 variation prompts.

Data & security notes
- For initial testing you can upload deidentified JSONL to the S3 path we provided, or we can accept a secure transfer via the Redwood private upload link. See attachment redwood_eval_dataset_spec.md for field/schema and optional PHI redaction checklist.
- All data during the pilot will be encrypted at rest and in transit; we can sign the NDAs and a short data processing addendum before full dataset transfer.

Scoring & thresholds
- Primary metric: normalized F1 on labeled entities (values & spans) with secondary human-assessed summary quality (1-5).
- Pass criteria (pilot): normalized entity F1 >= 0.78 AND average summary quality >= 4.0.
- We'll run automated scoring + a small blind human review (30 samples) to catch subtle regressions.

Deliverables & timeline
- 48–72 hour smoke test on 200 samples once dataset is uploaded.
- Full run (1,200 samples) within 7 business days of receiving complete dataset and access.
- Deliverables: raw scores, per-prompt error analysis, top failure buckets, recommended prompt/model tweaks, and a short handoff doc for your engineering team.

Next steps (action items)
1) Emily: confirm which transfer method you prefer (S3 share or Redwood secure upload) and whether you can start with 200 deidentified samples this week.
2) Karthik / Ben: internal prep — Ben will validate prompt bank and provide model-variant recommendations + expected run cost estimate.
3) Irene: schedule the technical onboarding call (30m) with SentryHealth engineers for Wednesday if that works.

Attachments: sentry_sample_prompts.csv (prompt bank), redwood_eval_dataset_spec.md (schema + upload instructions), pilot_timeline_and_scoring.xlsx (detailed scoring rubric).

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

—
Irene Choi

Emily / team — quick answers and recommendations below. Copying Emily so she has technical detail in thread.

PHI & required fields
- For entity scoring we need: note_id, note_text (deidentified), gold_entities (span + label), and optional metadata (encounter_type, note_timestamp). The spec in redwood_eval_dataset_spec.md shows exact JSONL fields we accept. Deidentification: removing direct identifiers (names, MRNs) is fine; keep clinical context (symptoms, medications) since that drives model behavior.

Threshold & path forward
- The 0.78 normalized F1 is a production-acceptable threshold. For a pilot baseline: expect Redwood-13B-fp16 to land between 0.70–0.80 depending on labeling consistency. If baseline is below target, we iterate in this order: 1) prompt tuning/prompt bank expansion (low cost), 2) run Redwood-13B with different sampling / beam settings, 3) try Redwood-13B-quant or Redwood-7B-quant for cost tradeoffs, 4) consider fine-tuning / instruction-tuning as next phase (only if needed).

Model & cost estimates (ballpark)
- Smoke test (200 samples): Redwood-13B-fp16 ~ $120–$220 (depending on sequence length / batch).
- Full 1,200 sample run: Redwood-13B-fp16 ~ $700–$1,200.
- If Sentry wants low-cost runs, Redwood-7B-quant typically reduces inference cost ~40–60% with a modest quality tradeoff. We'll include exact token-level cost after we see average sequence lengths.

Operational notes (upload and run)
- Pre-signed S3 upload is fine. We'll provide a time-limited PUT URL for the bucket path in related_links. Once uploaded, we kick off the eval job from the Redwood Console — you'll get a live job page with per-model progress and logs.

Scoring specifics
- Normalized F1: span overlap with label mapping + partial credit for boundary mismatches.
- Summary quality: we run a blind 30-sample human review (your SMEs or ours) using the attached pilot_timeline_and_scoring.xlsx rubric (1–5 scale).

Benchmark and examples
- Example benchmark runs and error buckets for a similar payer triage pilot: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/sentryhealth-2026 (contains per-prompt breakdowns).

I'll prepare a short run configuration file (model variants + batching settings + prompt templates) and share it in the next 2 hours so Irene can send it to Emily.
